note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: What do existing records establish about this oven, dryer or fryer recovery already provided and any unresolved residual supply for the named external heating-duty lead?

evidence.text: equipment D-A reads "D-A Product dryer A"
equipment W-1 reads "W-1 Facility wash hot water"
stream EX-A (asset stream:EX-A) reads "Dryer A exhaust"
equipment HX-S reads "HX-S Exhaust heat recovery exchanger"
D-A exhaust_temperature_C = 110; present; meaning and suitability unverified
D-A operating_window = "night"; present; meaning and suitability unverified
W-1 required_temperature_C = 50; present; meaning and suitability unverified
W-1 duty_basis = "unknown"; blank; meaning and suitability unverified
W-1 coincident_demand = "unknown"; blank; meaning and suitability unverified
W-1 operating_window = "day"; present; meaning and suitability unverified
W-1 alternative_heat_supply = "existing steam supply; comparative basis unknown"; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-S enabled = true; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-S source_revision = "C"; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-S coverage_claim = {"D-A": "unknown", "D-B": "unknown"}; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-S gas_compatibility = "corrosive/particulates unresolved"; present; meaning and suitability unverified
HX-S pressure_loss_basis = "unknown"; blank; meaning and suitability unverified

data_requests.item: Existing source routing, recovery-purpose and residual-supply basis
where: site records: approved existing exhaust routing, current recovery purpose, source revision/locator and coverage/bypass/availability records for this identified source
maintenance records: existing recovery operation, cleaning, fouling and unavailable/disabled records with equipment and period identity
data_requests.how: Separate own-inlet recovery from external-duty coverage. Retain full, partial, shared, zero and unknown claims literally; a recoverer label or nominal temperature does not establish actual residual transferable heat or allocate shared duty.

data_requests.item: Existing named-duty requirements and source/demand quantity and timing basis
where: site records: approved existing identity/purpose, temperature, heat-demand and operating schedules for the named duty, paired with source-period records where available, including quantities, locations, units, dates and responsible owners
data_requests.how: The anywhere-found duty is an unassociated lead, not a physical connection, nearby user or suitable sink. Review amount, thermal suitability and timing separately. A pair of nominal temperatures, common name or schedule mismatch does not by itself settle all practical alternatives or establish viability.

data_requests.item: Existing route, compatibility and alternative-heat constraints
where: site records: existing layout/distance and transport options; cleanliness/corrosion/particulate compatibility; condensation and pressure-loss/ventilation constraints; and the available alternative heating-supply and comparative basis
the vendor datasheet: applicable documented source and receiving-equipment limits, prior assessments and the qualified engineering review route
data_requests.how: Use the source/sink questions in S28 to identify what existing evidence supports or leaves unresolved. No universal temperature-difference threshold, mandatory field task, fixed sampling period or cost ranking is imposed. Qualified owners decide any further data plan and whether a study should proceed, be answered or be deferred.

questions.decision_rule: Review actual residual supply, named-duty amount/thermal requirements and coincident timing together with route losses, compatibility, condensation, pressure resistance and alternative heating basis. Distinguish documented working full coverage from unresolved partial, disabled, shared or internal-only recovery. A qualified company review can answer or defer the question from existing records; unknown evidence is not an automatic otherwise-close result, a feasible project or a mandate for a new project.

typical_benefit.wording: S28 (p. 1): "many companies install heat exchangers on the exhaust stacks of furnaces and ovens to produce hot water or to generate hot air for space heating." The same sheet: "The temperature difference between the primary and secondary process should be high enough (at least 200°F), and there should be a sufficient amount of usable waste heat." Fryers (S26, p. 107): "Heat can be recovered indirectly from a fryer's fat-laden exhaust gases via a heat exchange system and used for pre-heating air and water for use in other facility processes." No % stated.
source_titles: S28: DOE Industrial Technologies Program, Process Heating Tip Sheet #10, Using Waste Heat for External Processes (DOE/GO-102006-2225, Jan 2006)

S26: Masanet, Worrell, Graus and Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Fruit and Vegetable Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-59289-Revision, Mar 2008)

questions.limits: E31 addresses own-inlet/process-use recovery; it does not establish H6 external residual or duty coverage. The unchanged with-clause requires a named external duty somewhere in the model, not a nearby or connected sink. A supplied fully-covered working external claim may be quiet in new-opportunity triage; when shown here, its literal existing coverage and unverified basis must be acknowledged. The source-informed records-review policy does not impose a universal 200-degree threshold or authenticate supplied claims. Company engineering and safety/quality review govern feasibility and any actual work.
